claim: Simple Client::Get queries metadata before invoking descriptor-based Get; lookup failure returns before payload work.
Client::Create connects to the master and resolves configured storage before rpc_only returns without initializing Transfer Engine.
MountSegmentAndGetId validates overlap, registers memory, calls master mount, and only then records the local mounted segment UUID.
UnmountSegmentImpl withdraws capacity through the master before unregistering memory and erasing local bookkeeping.
TransferRequest source is the local buffer field for both READ and WRITE, whose direction is demonstrated by TCP write/read byte comparison.
In the TENT-capable facade, MC_USE_TENT or MC_USE_TEV1 selects TENT; installTransport logs a compatibility no-op in that mode.
Scatter waitFor timeout does not cancel transfer, buffers must remain alive, and destruction waits for physical completion.
Topology entries distinguish preferred and available HCAs; exact getDeviceIndex does not apply fallback selection.
Classic forced TCP requires compiled USE_TCP, while auto-discovery distinguishes EFA devices from ordinary RC RDMA.
Receiver locality tests use receiver-local NUMA/HCA relationships and do not compare NUMA IDs across hosts.
ReplicaStatus COMPLETE denotes available data; allocated replicas may begin directly in PROCESSING rather than visiting every enum state.
PutEnd verifies initiating client UUID and advances only eligible targeted replica types; completed-target retries are conditional no-ops.
General allocator permits nonempty best-effort allocation results below requested count, while strict named allocation prohibits kind fallback.
FailedPreferencesFallBackBestEffort expects two replicas from a request of three and never calls the excluded allocator.
Immutable Client::Put returns success on OBJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS after the defined dangling-local-disk healing attempt.
Flexible mode is exactly one memory and one NoF replica without DFS; finalization may End one type and revoke the other while succeeding.
DetermineFinalizeDecision separates expected allocation, successful transfers by medium, type-scoped End, and revoke decisions.
Query anchors client lease expiry to its steady-clock start before metadata RPC, plus returned TTL.
Descriptor Get selects for destination, releases hot-cache reference after transfer, handles transfer errors before checksum, then checks lease expiry.
Batch read tests assert copied bytes can still produce LEASE_EXPIRED and preserve TRANSFER_FAIL when both transfer and expiry fail.
Checksum test verifies 16 logical bytes in a 20-byte destination, ignores a trailing-byte mutation, and rejects a logical-byte mutation.
Client BufferHandle has allocator-owning and callback-backed view modes and is move-only.
PinnedBufferPool ordinary Acquire can fall back to pageable memory; AllocatePinned never does; cached buffer count is bounded.
Client liveness separates ACTIVE serving from SUSPECTED resource retention and terminal OFFLINE rejection.
Liveness tests start the suspicion window at actual transition and verify failed wrapped operations do not refresh or recover.
Reservation callback executes before OFFLINE publication, while retirement executes outside the transition mutex.
Grouped ObjectMetadata shares a Lease through the group index, so a member read can extend the shared eviction lease.
Evictor checks hard pinning and active lease before policy, and revalidates stale index candidates before reclaiming.
OffloadingReclaimer pins one queued memory source, records the task, and passes only other replica IDs to immediate inner release.
Offload tests distinguish rejected offload preservation from configured forced drops and count released bytes separately.
Effective master operation logging requires enable_ha, enable_oplog, and backend support.
Ordinary PutEnd publishes readable state and uses AppendOpLogVisibleBeforeDurable, logging queue failure rather than universally waiting for durability.
OrderedOpLogWriter exposes admission reservations, indivisible grouped commits, and durability futures independent of callbacks.
Snapshot writer verifies artifact size and CRC or readback, then manifest and descriptor, and attempts candidate-prefix cleanup on failure.
Snapshot publication requires maintenance ownership and transactional backend support separately from artifact writing.
Rebootstrap builds candidate metadata, replays durable suffix, rechecks compaction floor, and preserves installed state until safe replacement.
Restore tests verify remount range identity, skip size-invalid object descriptors, and fail closed on ambiguous overlapping ranges.
StandbyObjectMetadata deliberately omits read leases and runtime soft pins, while representing hard pin metadata separately.
Raw tensor binding reads device metadata through accelerator abstraction, validates size/overflow, and retains original addresses for staging/IPC.
Store-observed cache reuse metrics are explicitly distinguished from end-to-end request/token hit ratios.
Optional vLLM Store keys include model, rank/group namespaces and format/deployment prefixes before chunk hash.
Optional vLLM sender synchronizes producer events before Store put, receiver maps per-key negative results to block errors, and registration changes require drained transfers.
Rank-local padding test copies logical single-block lengths while a two-block contiguous span retains intervening page padding.
Sleep/wake registration tests preserve host registrations, renew device ranges idempotently, and retry unresolved failures.
